selection.rule: The five largest total primary energy producers in the world, excluding Russia.
selection.source: U.S. EIA International Energy Statistics, total primary energy production, 2024
selection.caveat: Canada and India differ by about 1% and swap order in the Energy Institute Statistical Review for the same year. The set of five is stable across both sources; the order within it is not, and the dashboard does not display one.

comparability_statement: Each country is measured on its own terms. Event counts reflect what is publicly reported under that country's reporting rules, not how often disruption happens. A country with fewer recorded events is not shown to be safer, more resilient or less disrupted. Figures are not comparable across countries and are never ranked.

reporting_environments.mandatory_regulatory: Operators must report qualifying outages to a regulator, and many of those reports are public.
reporting_environments.mixed_regulatory: Some outage reporting is mandatory and public; much is not, and press and company statements fill the gap.
reporting_environments.corporate_disclosure: Disruption is disclosed mainly through company and ministry statements, usually only when material to investors or the state.
reporting_environments.media_only: Operators and authorities do not publish event-level outage reports. Events come from media and company statements, so most smaller disruptions will not appear.
reporting_environments.conflict_restricted: Disruption is reported under wartime restrictions by the authorities concerned, so independent, attacker-side and open-source reporting carry most of the record.

order: alphabetical by name; never by any figure
